claims: President Donald Trump fired U.S. Attorney General Pam Bondi on April 2, 2026.
Pam Bondi's tenure as U.S. Attorney General lasted 14 months.
Bondi faced pressure over the Department of Justice's handling of Epstein-related documents.
Bondi failed to prevent the public release of sensitive, high-profile names in Epstein-related documents.
Trump was consistently frustrated that Bondi did not move quickly or effectively enough to investigate and indict his political enemies, such as Letitia James and James Comey.
Trump complained frequently to allies about Bondi's performance.
The decision to fire Bondi followed her failure to secure a graceful exit.
Bondi's firing followed the removal of other cabinet members.
Todd Blanche was named as the acting attorney general following Bondi's departure.
